messages:
maria: heads up — eu-west2 rack-7 showing a weird packing pattern, lots of 1-GPU pods stranded on three nodes, scheduler keeps leaving 2xGPU holes.
ajay: hmm, any taints or affinity changes recently?
maria: no taints. noticed intermittent network tx drops on the nodes, pods get evicted then reschedule nearby but not packed.
devin: can you paste the scheduler/binder errors?
maria: ```
I0315 14:12:03.123456 1 scheduler.go:345] binding pod default/model-train-abc to node gpu-eu-west2-7a
I0315 14:12:03.128000 1 scheduler.go:367] preemption skip: candidate nodes filtered
I0315 14:12:05.500000 1 binder.go:88] failed to bind: network timeout
```
jen: that looks like short kubelet/CRI timeouts — scheduler treats node as flakey and avoids it, which fragments the binpack across racks.
ajay: could be the NIC driver reset we saw in us-west last month. same symptoms.
maria: did a quick experiment — cordoned the two worst nodes and re-ran a defrag job, fragmentation dropped ~40%.
devin: soft-evict + graceful drain (30s) instead of cordon might be less disruptive. what happened when you tried soft-evict?
maria: soft-evict helped locally, but the autoscaler then spun up mixed-size nodes and introduced uneven slots again.
jen: short-term: add scheduler preference for nodes with net-health=ok annotation so the scheduler biases toward stable NICs. medium-term: patch NIC firmware on rack-7.
ajay: +1. also recommend bumping consolidation threshold for eu-west2 for next autoscaler cycle.
maria: opening an incident with logs and cluster metrics, tagging @sre-bot to create the ticket.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4492 - eu-west2 rack-7 NIC flaps. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-4492 :white_check_mark:
ajay: cool — plan: canary firmware push 03:00 UTC tomorrow, then run defrag script and monitor tokenized packing metrics for 2h.
maria: noted. will include node list and kubelet logs in the ticket and follow up after canary.
